responsive-breakpoint-order-desync/case-.mechanism: @media (max-width:600px) reassigns flexbox order (.step--payment{order:1}, .step--shipping{order:2}, .step--review{order:3}) so the steps stack visually as Payment, Shipping, Review while the DOM source order stays the correct process order Shipping, Payment, Review. Each step's number is a hard-coded static badge (<span class="step__num" aria-hidden="true">) glued to its content rather than a CSS counter() keyed to visual position, so on mobile the badges travel with their steps and render out of order ('2' Payment above '1' Shipping), visually asserting that payment precedes shipping. A screen reader follows the correct DOM/tab order, so visual order diverges from the meaningful source order at the ≤600px viewport.
responsive-breakpoint-order-desync/case-.scenario: E-commerce 3-step checkout wizard (Shipping → Payment → Review) with hard-coded step badges; a max-width:600px flexbox order: reorder stacks Payment above Shipping on mobile, so the badges read out of order ('2' above '1') and the visual order contradicts the meaningful DOM source order.
responsive-breakpoint-order-desync/case-.note: Scenario claimed the visible step numbers are CSS counter() values keyed to visual position, producing a clean renumbered '1 Payment, 2 Shipping, 3 Review' on mobile. The actual HTML hard-codes the numerals as static <span class="step__num" aria-hidden="true"> text (1 on Shipping, 2 on Payment, 3 on Review) pinned to their content, so mobile actually shows badges out of order ('2 Payment' above '1 Shipping'). The breakpoint (max-width:600px) and the order: declarations in primarySelector are correct; only the numbering mechanism and the described mobile read are wrong. Defect (visual-order desync) is genuinely present.
